$comment: Gzip byte ceilings for scripts/check-size.mjs (esbuild bundle, production condition, min+gzip). Measured 2026-06-09: core-counter 5651 B, scaffold-counter 5754 B (audit's real vite-scaffold counter measured 7.10 KB). Ceilings = measured reality rounded up to the next 64 B; raise only deliberately, in the same PR as the growth. Headroom is deliberately small, so a raise is a decision rather than a drift. core-counter is set from its 2026-07-27 measurement of 6512 B, having accounted for all 781 B of growth over 63a896a commit by commit: 557 B bought Critical and High fixes (URL and handler sanitization, the compiled children protocol, Suspense, hydration and redirect correctness), 18 B was a signal-write perf trade, and the other 206 B is esbuild alone declining to tree-shake Suspense and ErrorBoundary past their _deferChildren markers, which Rollup drops.

core-counter.$raise-2026-08-15: 6528 -> 6592 for the 0.12.4 correctness release. Measured 6529 B, i.e. it went over by ONE byte, so the ceiling moves to the next 64 B boundary as the convention above requires. Growth over the 6512 B baseline is 17 B, against 1836 changed lines of packages/core/src. Almost all of that release tree-shakes out of a counter app entirely (data.js, form.js, a11y.js and animation.js are never reached by an app that imports signal/h/mount), so the residue is the code every app pulls in: spread() gaining the `ref` case it was missing, the boundary branches in hydrateNode, and flushScheduler re-arming a frame when a callback schedules work during a flush. 17 B for a release that closes a validation library failing open and a hydration path that duplicated nodes is a trade worth making explicitly.
core-counter.$raise-2026-08-28: 6592 -> 6656 for the conditional-list teardown fix. Measured 6631 B, so the ceiling moves to the next 64 B boundary as the convention above requires. Growth over the 6592 B ceiling is 39 B and over the 6549 B measurement 82 B, all of it in dom.js: the start marker that brackets an embedded list, and _liveRegionNodes, which walks that bracket when a region is torn down. The render.js half of the fix costs a counter app nothing, because the hydrate path tree-shakes out of one. What the 82 B buys is a region that removes the list it is holding: before it, hiding a conditional whose list had grown left every row added since mount in the page, and showing it again rendered a second list beside the orphans, permanently. There is no cheaper way to describe content that manages itself than a pair of markers, since a list of nodes is stale the moment the inner effect runs again.
core-counter.description: what-core runtime imported by a typical h()-based counter app (production condition)

scaffold-counter.description: create-what vanilla template counter (src/main.jsx equivalent) via what-framework + runtime JSX (production condition); ceiling 7.8 KB covers the audit-measured 7.10 KB real-scaffold build + ~10%
